intelligence.human_view: The count bubble was the stuck-on disc from the A4 eye — a purple disc straddling the tile's corner, half outside, reading as stuck on. The ball fixes it by being part of the tile: black obsidian, white number, sitting inside, never on the corner — and lit around it in the tile's own color, so the rim light ties it to its tile the way the tile's own rim ties it to the page. A ball, not a disc stuck on; inside, not half outside; the tile's color, not a stranger's. That is the notification done the way the whole system is done: a real object, inside its place, lit in its own color. And it closes a loop from 23:00Z: the badge was the one part of the tiles he had not seen — now he has not only seen it, he has designed it, and his design is the build.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a little black ball with a white number on it, sitting neatly inside a tile — like a jewel set into a ring, not stuck on the outside like a sticker. And a pretty light glows around the ball in the same color as the tile it sits on, so it belongs there. Never hanging off the corner, never half outside — inside, where it belongs.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, the little number that tells you how many new things there are should be a black ball with a white number, sitting neatly inside the tile — never stuck on the corner like a label hanging off. And a gentle light glows around it in the color of the tile it sits on, so it looks like it belongs there. A ball, inside, lit in its own color.
intelligence.naya_view: A BLACK OBSIDIAN BALL WITH A WHITE NUMBER, INTEGRATED INSIDE THE TILE, NEVER STUCK ON THE CORNER, LIT UP AROUND IT IN THE COLOR OF WHATEVER TILE IT SITS ON.
